issues.legal_issue: The restriction on partition of a family dwelling house applies when an intestate leaves one male Class I heir and one or more female Class I heirs.
material_facts: The dispute concerned a partition claim by a daughter against her brother, the sole surviving male heir, and other heirs of an intestate Hindu.
The Court considered whether the plural wording referring to male heirs in the special dwelling-house provision excluded a case with only one male heir.
issues.conclusion: The restriction applies even where there is only one male Class I heir. While that heir continues to retain the property as the family dwelling house, the female heir's right to claim partition is postponed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23 of the Hindu Succession Act is a special exception to the ordinary rules of succession and partition, intended to preserve the family dwelling house and prevent its fragmentation. The Court applied Section 13(2) of the General Clauses Act, under which the plural may include the singular where the context permits, and approved the approach of the Calcutta High Court in Arun Kumar Sanyal v. Jnanendra Nath Sanyal, Surya Kumar Das v. Maya Dutta and Usha Mazumdar v. Smriti Basu, as well as the related view in Mookkammal v. Chitravadivammal, Janabi Ammal v. T.S.A. Palani Mudaliar, Ponnuswamy v. Meenakshi Ammal and Purnawasi v. Sukhadevi. It rejected the contrary approach in Hemalata Devi v. Umasankari Moharana and Kariyavva v. Hanumantappa Mallurappa.

rule.if: partition_action and intestate_class_i_gender_mix and sole_male_heir and family_dwelling_house_occupied and male_heir_retains_home

predicates.partition_action: A claimant seeks partition of property inherited from a Hindu intestate.
predicates.intestate_class_i_gender_mix: The intestate left surviving both male and female heirs in the first class of heirs.
predicates.sole_male_heir: Only one surviving first-class male heir is involved.
predicates.family_dwelling_house_occupied: The property is a dwelling house occupied by members of the intestate's family.
predicates.male_heir_retains_home: The male heir continues to retain the property as the family's dwelling house and has not chosen to divide it or otherwise ceased to retain it in that capacity.

issues.definition: When a partition action concerns an occupied family dwelling house inherited by both male and female first-class heirs, and the sole male heir retains it as the family home, the female heir's claim to partition is postponed.

issues.legal_issue: A house let to a tenant and no longer occupied by the intestate's family is not protected from partition as a family dwelling house under the special restriction.
material_facts: The property at issue was occupied by a tenant, rather than by any of the intestate's heirs.
The daughter sought partition, and the sole male heir relied on the special restriction concerning dwelling houses.
The male heir had let the house to a stranger and had not pleaded that the letting resulted from extenuating or involuntary circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The house was not protected from partition by the special restriction. The daughter's partition claim could proceed, and the appeal against the preliminary decree was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23 protects a dwelling house occupied by members of the intestate's family, not merely a residential building that is tenanted. The majority treated the male heir's voluntary letting of the house to a stranger as conduct showing that he had ceased to retain it as the family home; it distinguished temporary absence caused by work or other compulsion. Justice Punchhi likewise concluded that a tenanted house is not a dwelling house in the provision's relevant sense. The Court also referred to Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act and to the purpose of Section 23 in preserving the family home.

rule.if: partition_action and tenant_in_possession and family_not_in_occupation and voluntary_letting and no_extenuating_circumstances_pleaded

predicates.partition_action: A claimant seeks partition of property inherited from a Hindu intestate.
predicates.tenant_in_possession: A tenant occupies the property under a letting by an heir.
predicates.family_not_in_occupation: No member of the intestate's family occupies the property as the family home.
predicates.voluntary_letting: The male heir let the property to a stranger rather than retaining it for occupation by the family.
predicates.no_extenuating_circumstances_pleaded: The male heir did not plead that the letting occurred because of circumstances beyond his control.

issues.definition: When a tenant occupies a property that the family no longer occupies as its home, and the male heir voluntarily let it without pleading circumstances explaining the letting, the special restriction does not bar the female heir's partition claim.
